## The connectivity map first

`high_fan_in_fan_out` fires on two different problems, and they demand opposite responses. The percentile cutoffs in the evidence make the split visible: fan-in p95 = 9 / p99 = 10; fan-out p95 = 6 / p99 = 11.

| File | fan-in | fan-out | Also charged with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/utils.ts` | **18** (≫ p99) | 1 | God File 425 L, 7× sync I/O |
| `src/plugin.ts` | **10** (= p99) | 3 | God Function `buildFinished` 103 L |
| `src/log.ts` | 9 (= p95) | 0 | 2 unprefixed booleans |
| `test/utils.ts` | 9 (= p95) | 0 | 1 sync read (test tier) |
| `src/index.ts` | 4 | **17** (≫ p99) | God File 460 L, `build` 293 L |
| `src/esbuild/index.ts` | 1 | **11** (= p99) | `runEsbuild` 237 L (4.0×) |
| `src/rollup.ts` | 0 | 7 | `getRollupConfig` 122 L, False Identity |
| `src/api-extractor.ts` | 1 | 6 | `rollupDtsFiles` 85 L |

**Fan-in is the blast-radius number.** Only files other modules import can ripple outward. Fan-out means the file is an orchestrator — big and hard to read, but its edits go nowhere. Since the question is "reduce blast radius *across* the codebase," the fan-in column drives the order.

## Triage order

**1 — `src/utils.ts` (fan-in 18, God File 425 L)**
The only file in the repo past the p99 fan-in cutoff, at double it. 18 modules import a 425-line grab bag, so every one of them takes a context hit and an edit-collision risk for functions it never touches. It's also the cheapest hub to break up: fan-out 1 means it depends on almost nothing, and `test_gap: 0` on `crime_00039`/`crime_00044` says it's covered, so a split is verifiable.

One condition: split *and repoint the importers*. Leaving `utils.ts` as a re-export barrel preserves the 18-way fan-in and buys nothing — you'd have moved the code without moving the coupling.

**2 — `src/plugin.ts` (fan-in 10, `buildFinished` 103 L)**
Sits exactly at p99 fan-in with 29 transitive importers, and carries `agent_risk 0.54` — the highest single score in all 87 findings. The reason is the combination: load-bearing for 10 importers *and* `test_gap: 0.75`, i.e. a 103-line class method with essentially nothing protecting it. Ten importers on a plugin surface is legitimate, so don't split the file — extract helpers out of `buildFinished`, and get a test on it before you do.

**3 — `src/index.ts` (fan-out 17, God File 460 L)**
Past the fan-out p99 of 11, and the largest bodies in the repo. But note `crime_00023/24/25` are nested, not three problems: `build` 167–459 wraps an anonymous arrow 183–456 which wraps `mainTasks` 260–453. That's **one** ~293-line body reported at three depths. With fan-in 4 this is a local comprehension fix, not a blast-radius fix — real value, lower leverage. `test_gap: 0` makes the extraction safe to attempt.

**4 — `src/esbuild/index.ts` (fan-out 11, `runEsbuild` 237 L = 4.0×)**
Same shape as #3 and same reasoning: fan-in 1, so nobody downstream benefits. What earns it a slot is `crime_00040` — a 38-property options bag threaded through a 237-line body. That's the specific thing that makes an agent edit one branch and silently break another. Covered by tests (`test_gap: 0`).

**5 — `src/esbuild/postcss.ts`**
Two high-severity God Functions (`postcssPlugin` 140 L wrapping `setup` 18–143 — again nested, one body), untested at 0.75, plus Return Shape Roulette with **0% key overlap** between `{ namespace, path }` and `{ contents, loader }`. Only 7 transitive importers, no fan-in charge, so it's containment work rather than blast-radius work.

## Leave alone

- **`src/log.ts`** — fan-in 9 looks alarming next to `utils.ts`, but fan-out 0 and the only charges are two unprefixed booleans. A logger imported by 9 modules is a shared leaf working as intended; high fan-in here is health, not debt. Splitting it churns 9 importers to remove no risk. Treat as load-bearing, leave the code.
- **`docs/README.md`** — the one *high*-severity God File (679 L, 2.3×), and still not a refactor target: `blast_radius: 0`, `agent_risk: 0.27`. The God File charge doesn't carry the same meaning for prose as for a module. Split it for documentation reasons if you want; it buys zero risk reduction.
- **`src/rollup.ts`** — high-severity `getRollupConfig` (122 L), but `blast_radius_importers: 0` — nothing imports it. Its fan-out 7 is outbound. Worth the two-minute rename from `crime_00009` (a `get*` name that calls `setSilent` and `removeFiles` is a trap for an agent), but it doesn't belong in a blast-radius plan.
- **`src/cli-main.ts`** — `main` at 153 L is high severity with only 2 importers. Entry points are allowed to be long orchestrators.
- **`test/utils.ts`** — fan-in 9, but `tier: nonDomain`. Test-harness coupling isn't production blast radius.

## One caveat on the evidence

Every finding in this report has `churn: 0` and `recency: 0` — the git-history signal is absent, so this ranking is purely structural. If real history existed, a moderately-connected file with heavy bug-fix churn could reasonably outrank `src/plugin.ts`. Worth re-running against a repo with history before committing to the order.
